questions.q: Where do raw AI source documents — PDFs, transcripts, images — typically land first on Azure?
options: Directly inside an Azure AI Search index
Blob Storage, inside a container
Azure Key Vault
An Azure OpenAI deployment
questions.explain: Blob Storage is the landing zone for raw documents — cheap, durable, and unaware of any later embedding step.

questions.q: Does Blob Storage itself know or care that a file will eventually be turned into an embedding?
options: No — it just holds the raw blob; embedding happens in a separate step, written to a different store
Yes — every blob is automatically embedded on upload
Only if the container is named 'embeddings'
Yes, but only for image files
questions.explain: Blob Storage is purely a raw-file store; embeddings get generated and written somewhere else entirely, like a search index.

questions.q: Where do embeddings themselves actually get stored once they're generated?
options: Back in the same Blob Storage container as the source file
In a search index's schema, in a dedicated vector field
In Azure Key Vault secrets
They aren't stored — they're regenerated on every query
questions.explain: A search index like Azure AI Search defines a vector field specifically for storing an embedding, queryable by similarity.

questions.q: What does a vector field let you query that a plain text field doesn't?
options: Exact keyword matches only
Results ranked purely by file upload date
Similarity — finding content that means something similar, not just text that matches literally
Nothing different — they behave identically
questions.explain: Vector fields enable similarity search, finding semantically related content rather than requiring an exact keyword match.

questions.q: In the index Fields screenshot, what does the 'Vector index quota usage' panel indicate?
options: That vector storage is billed and limited separately from the plain-text fields in the same index
That the index has no vector fields defined at all
The total number of documents in the storage account
The current Azure subscription's spending limit
questions.explain: That panel is a reminder that vector storage has its own quota and cost, tracked apart from the index's regular text fields.
